accent-dark.note: Legacy token, no longer referenced by any component after the WCAG contrast pass — accent-text replaced its role for eyebrow/link text, and accent-fill replaced it for button hover. Kept defined for backward compatibility; candidate for removal in a later cleanup.

accent-text.note: WCAG-driven derivative of accent (#2DCC8F, 1.97:1 as text — fails AA). Light mode only: #1B7955 (4.5:1+ against page/surface bg). Flattens to accent's #2DCC8F in dark mode, which already clears 9:1 there.

accent-text-large.note: Second, lighter WCAG stop reserved for the Metric Display only (≥32px/700, qualifies for the 3:1 large-text threshold instead of 4.5:1). Light mode: #21976A (3.50:1, +17% margin). Flattens to accent's #2DCC8F in dark mode.

accent-fill.note: #1B7955, same value as accent-text but does NOT flatten in dark mode — it's the button-fill background under white text, a bg-independent pairing (white-on-#2DCC8F fails at 2.07:1 regardless of theme). Constant across both themes.

accent-fill-hover.note: #145C40. Darker pressed/hover state for accent-fill (7.97:1 white-on-fill). Constant across both themes, same reasoning as accent-fill.

accent-chip.note: #186D4C (L26%, darker than accent-text's L29%). The category chip's own rgba(45,204,143,0.15) backdrop composites lighter than the page/surface background, eating into accent-text's margin (down to ~4.2:1 on the surface-backed variant — under AA). accent-chip was calibrated against the worse of the two composited chip backgrounds: 4.94:1 there, 5.36:1 against the page-bg variant. Flattens to accent (#2DCC8F) in dark mode, where the chip already clears 6-7:1 untreated.

display.purpose: Hero headline and case-study title only. Appears exactly once per page.

headline.purpose: Section-level statements and hub-page h1s: Contact title, /work and /blog index, blog post title, case-study 'next project' link.

title.purpose: Card titles, phase titles, sub-headings inside long-form content, the NDA password-gate heading.

body.purpose: Long-form paragraph copy: case-study context, mdx-prose, phase descriptions, bullets, subtitles.

caption.purpose: Compact sentence-case UI copy: card descriptions, nav/footer links, CTA links, pill-button labels. Introduced during the typeset pass to separate this from Body's long-form job.

label.purpose: Uppercase section eyebrows (headers, not captions) and form error text.

tag.purpose: The smallest supporting text: category chips, metadata labels, phase numbers, date stamps. Introduced during the typeset pass to separate this from Label's section-header job.

shadows.name: card-ambient
shadows.purpose: Resting-state shadow on project cards only, in light mode. Never grows on hover.

shadows.name: card-ambient-dark
shadows.purpose: Dark-mode equivalent of card-ambient; deliberately fainter.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition timing for color/background/border-color changes site-wide (200ms).

motion.name: ease-out-entrance
motion.purpose: Framer Motion fadeUp entrance used on nearly every section and card (translate-y 20-30px + opacity, 0.5-0.6s).

narrative.overview:
The site reads like a working notebook, not a showreel: one disciplined accent color, one typeface, flat surfaces, and generous air between ideas. Every visual choice defers to the content it's carrying — a case-study metric, a phase description, a piece of reasoning — rather than competing with it. This is deliberate: the audience is hiring managers judging design judgment, and a portfolio that visually overperforms its own restraint would undercut the argument it's trying to make.

Density is low and rhythm is slow. Sections breathe at 96px of vertical space on desktop (64px on mobile), so each idea — a hero claim, a result, a piece of process — gets its own uninterrupted beat before the next one starts. Nothing competes with the mint accent for attention: it is reserved for what's interactive or worth noticing (CTAs, active nav state, links, the oversized result metrics), and everywhere else the palette stays neutral paper-and-ink.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, used sparingly and consistently, never a second hue
Flat by default; hover states shift color and scale, never elevation
Pill-shaped buttons and chips everywhere; soft (12–16px) radii on content containers
Slow vertical rhythm (96px/64px) that treats whitespace as a structural tool, not a gap
Bilingual (ES/EN) and dual-theme (light/dark) by construction — no visual decision is made for one language or one theme alone

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: The accent is the only hue used to mean "interactive" or "notice this." It never appears as decoration, and no second accent hue is introduced, even for a single component. Four lightness stops of the same hue (accent, accent-text, accent-text-large, accent-fill) don't violate this — it's still one voice, calibrated to stay legible everywhere it speaks.

rules.name: The Text-Safe Mint Rule
rules.body: Never color text directly with accent (#2DCC8F) — it fails WCAG AA against every background in the light theme (1.97:1 vs the 4.5:1 required). Text and text-bearing fills route through accent-text (small/body text, 4.5:1), accent-text-large (Metric Display only, 3:1), or accent-fill/accent-fill-hover (button backgrounds under white text, theme-invariant). Reserve bare accent for borders, icons, and non-text fills only.

rules.name: The Ink-for-Headers Rule
rules.body: Any title, section label, or element functioning as a heading — including small uppercase eyebrows — uses text-primary (Ink), never text-secondary, regardless of size or visual weight.

rules.name: The Flat Accent Rule
rules.body: In dark mode, accent-dark, accent-text, accent-text-large, and accent-chip all collapse to the same value as accent (#2DCC8F) — dark mode already clears every contrast requirement at full strength, so there's no dimmed dark-mode variant. accent-fill/accent-fill-hover are the exception: they stay constant across both themes because their constraint (white text on top) doesn't depend on page background.

rules.name: The Eyebrow-Is-a-Header Rule
rules.body: A Label-role element is a header, not a caption, even at 13px. It follows the Ink-for-Headers color rule without exception.

rules.name: The Caption/Tag Split Rule
rules.body: Caption (14px) is for compact sentence-case UI copy that still reads like prose — descriptions, links, button labels. Tag (11px) is for the smallest supporting text riding along another element — a card's category, a data value's own label, a date stamp. If it could stand alone as a sentence, it's Caption; if it's decoration/metadata, it's Tag.

rules.name: The Border-Over-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Hover/focus states never grow a shadow. A card's hover state is a border-color shift plus a subtle image scale; a nav link's active state is a color change. Reach for border-color or the accent first, shadow last.

dos: Do use the accent hue as the only color signaling "interactive" or "important" — CTAs, active nav, links, result metrics, category eyebrows — but through the correct stop: accent-text for small/body text, accent-text-large for the Metric Display only, accent-fill/accent-fill-hover for button backgrounds, and bare accent for borders/icons/non-text fills.
Do keep every title, label, and eyebrow in text-primary, even when small or uppercase; text-secondary is for genuine secondary content only.
Do hold vertical rhythm at 96px (desktop) / 64px (mobile) between major sections and case-study blocks.
Do use pill shape (999px) for every button and chip, and 12–16px soft-rectangle radii for every content container.
Do signal hover/active state with border-color, text-color, or scale — never with added or deepened shadow.
Do reserve fixed two-line height for card descriptions so grid cards stay aligned regardless of copy length.
Do design every new surface bilingually (ES/EN) and theme-aware (light/dark) from the start, not as a retrofit.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue, even for a single one-off component. (Four lightness stops of the same hue is fine; a second hue is not.)

Don't color text directly with bare accent (#2DCC8F) — it fails WCAG AA against every light-mode background and as a white-text button fill in both themes. Always route through accent-text, accent-text-large, or accent-fill.
Don't add a drop shadow beyond the existing faint ambient card shadow; no shadow-based hover elevation anywhere in the system.
Don't hardcode colors in components outside the CSS-variable token system, except the scoped, intentional #E53E3E error state.

Don't use a circular avatar or profile-style imagery within the page; photo frames follow the same 16px soft-rectangle language as everything else. (The favicon is exempt as platform chrome, not page content.)
Don't write Tailwind v4-only syntax or config; the project is pinned to Tailwind v3.
